Tags.rationale: NibbitsWeak.Tags => [EncounterTag.Nibbit] (NibbitsWeak.cs:10). Not modeled on the sim's Encounter dataclass itself; rooms.py:177 (_overgrowth_rooms's tags dict) carries tags['nibbits_weak']=('nibbit',) -- same single tag, feeding the same tag-safe grab-bag picker (rooms.py:330-344, :458-475) that mirrors ActModel.AddWithoutRepeatingTags. Run-layer picker mechanism (seam/rooms_and_map, out of scope for this record beyond confirming the transcription).

RoomType.rationale: NibbitsWeak.RoomType => RoomType.Monster (NibbitsWeak.cs:12) -- IsWeak is orthogonal to RoomType; both are Monster-room encounters. Sim carries no room_type field on the Encounter dataclass; 'nibbits_weak' is placed in rooms.py:144-147's weak_keys for _overgrowth_rooms() (seam/rooms_and_map owns the picker itself). GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) matches EncounterModel.cs:70/89's Monster=>10/20 defaults, which NibbitsWeak does not override.

IsWeak.maps_to: ENCOUNTERS['nibbits_weak'] listed in rooms.py weak_keys (pool membership, not a field on the Encounter dataclass)
IsWeak.rationale: NibbitsWeak.IsWeak => true (NibbitsWeak.cs:14). Its only reader in the whole decompiled tree is ActModel.AllWeakEncounters/AllRegularEncounters (ActModel.cs:149/154), a pure Monster-room pool-membership filter with no other consequence -- confirmed by `grep -rn '\.IsWeak\b' src` returning only that one call site plus the declarations themselves. The sim reproduces the ONLY observable effect structurally instead of via a field: 'nibbits_weak' is placed directly in rooms.py:144-147's weak_keys tuple rather than the normal_keys tuple, so it is drawn from (and only from) the weak pool exactly as AllWeakEncounters filters it. Deliberately-different representation, identical result.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim counterpart. C#'s only consumers of AllPossibleMonsters are ActModel.AllMonsters (ActModel.cs:169, read only by ModelDb.Monsters -> UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68/147's dev-console 'monsters' listing and NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164's stats-screen ratio label) and the Bestiary screen (NBestiary.cs:194) -- all UI/dev-console, zero gameplay or RNG effect, confirmed by reading every caller in src/. The headless sim has neither surface, so omitting a counterpart costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: NibbitsWeak.GenerateMonsters (NibbitsWeak.cs:18-23) constructs one Nibbit, sets `.IsAlone = true`, and returns a single-element list with a null slot -- zero base.Rng calls. NIBBITS_WEAK.monster_classes=[partial(Nibbit, is_alone=True)], no slots/monster_slots set (defaults (), matching the null slot) and create_monsters draws no RNG for composition (the default implementation this encounter inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py). Roster (1x Nibbit, is_alone=True), order (trivial), slot (null/none on both sides) and draw count (0 == 0) all match. (Unlike nibbits_normal, no Slots override exists in C# here at all -- NibbitsWeak inherits EncounterModel's default empty Slots -- so there is no slot-declaration gap to file for this unit.)

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: (structural -- Encounter dataclass has no hook methods)
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by NibbitsWeak. The sim's Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) declares no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register -- it is plain data, structurally incapable of joining the hook walk, which reproduces 'the encounter itself is not a listener' exactly.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward gold ladder (the encounter brief's 5th thing to verdict)
guards.rationale: NibbitsWeak does not override MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, so both inherit EncounterModel.cs:64-100's RoomType ladder (Monster=10-20) times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under AscensionLevel.Poverty. NIBBITS_WEAK carries min_gold=None, max_gold=None (Encounter dataclass default, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so rewards.py:886-887 falls back to GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) -- the same ladder. Ascension (Poverty) scaling is out of scope by the audit contract (rewards.py:32's explicit 'no Scarcity/Poverty scaling').

guards.what: EncounterModel.Rng independence (per the encounter brief: verify the sim does not draw encounter rolls off a shared/run-level stream)
guards.rationale: NibbitsWeak.GenerateMonsters makes zero base.Rng calls (NibbitsWeak.cs:18-23, confirmed by reading the whole method) and the sim's create_monsters counterpart (the default Encounter.create_monsters this unit inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) makes zero calls to any Rng/random.Random for composition -- there is nothing here for stream identity to diverge on. (Draw-count fact only; which named stream backs EncounterModel.Rng in general is seam/rng_streams' mechanism, already verdicted faithful for the seeding formula at rng_streams step 21.)
